title: pvTemporalInterpolator
body:
## pvTemporalInterpolator

Linearly interpolates point coordinates and point and cell arrays between the two stored time steps around a requested time, so data can be obtained at times the input did not save; ParaView uses vtkAdaptiveTemporalInterpolator, which also copes when the mesh appears to change between steps. By ParaView default it reports the input's own steps; DiscreteTimeStepInterval reports evenly spaced steps instead and ResampleFactor adds steps inside each stored interval. The input needs at least two time steps, and interpolated values are a linear approximation, not solver results.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Schemaxis updates every node at the scene time, and the curated foam reader rejects times it has not stored (TIME_UNAVAILABLE), so intermediate scene times are refused at a foam node before this filter runs.
- Linear interpolation smooths over events between saved steps; save output more often when such detail matters.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `TemporalInterpolator`. Identity: `filters/TemporalInterpolator`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input of the Temporal Interpolator. Accepted data: any data object (vtkDataObject). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":true,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataObject"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DiscreteTimeStepInterval` | If Discrete Time Step Interval is set to 0, then the Temporal Interpolator will provide a continuous region of time on its output. If set to anything else, then the output will define a finite set of time points on its output, each spaced by the Discrete Time Step Interval. The output will have (time range)/(discrete time step interval) time steps. (Note that the time range is defined by the time range of the data of the input filter, which may be different from other pipeline objects or the range defined in the animation inspector.) This is a useful option to use if you have a dataset with one missing time step and wish to 'fill in' the missing data with an interpolated value from the steps on either side. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `ResampleFactor` | When ResampleFactor is a non zero positive integer, each pair of input time steps will be interpolated between with the number of steps specified. For example an input of 1,2,3,4,5 and a resample factor of 10, will produce steps 0f 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, ..., 1.9, 2.0. Irregular input steps will produce irregular output steps. Resample factor will only be used if DiscreteTimeStepInterval is zero, otherwise the DiscreteTimeStepInterval takes precedence | `{"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvTemporalInterpolator",
  "inputs": {
    "Input": "UPSTREAM_Input"
  }
}
```
